prerequisites: Basic knowledge of calculus, linear algebra and physics

learning_outcomes.text: To know the basic theory of solid and structural mechanics
To know and embrace the concepts of stress state, strain state, constitutive relationship
To understand relations governing the internal action and the elastic curve of a beam
To understand the response of beam elements under tension/compression, bending, shear, and torsion
To be able to apply the basic concepts of solid and structural mechanics
To be able to draw of the internal action diagrams for beams, for given load and constrain conditions
To be able to evaluate the deflection of a beam, for given load and constrain conditions
To be able to calculate the stress state of a beam subjected to tension/compression, bending, shear, and torsion
To be able to calculate critical loads for compressed beams
To be able to use the acquired knowledge for autonomously studying issues related to solid and structural mechanics
To evaluate the applicability of structural models to describe real structures and elements
To evaluate the applicability of the beam theory
To assess and compare independently the engineering solutions of a structural problem
Choosing autonomously the right approach and the appropriate tools to solve a structural problem
To communicate effectively in written and oral form in the context of solid and structural mechanics
To know and know how to use the specific scientific / technical terminology of solid and structural mechanics
To be able to properly use the mathematical language to describe the treated issues
To catalog, schematize and elaborate the acquired knowledge
To correlate the different topics one other and with the basic and related disciplines
To autonomously use and apply the acquired knowledge

syllabus_topics: Principles of rigid body mechanics: Forces and moments
Forces and moments transmitted by beam elements: Beam element concept
Forces and moments transmitted by beams
Stress, strain, and constitutive relations: Stress analysis
Beams under axial load: The semi-inverse method by de Saint-Venant
The semi-inverse method for beams under axial load
Beams under torsion: Torsion of circular cross-sections
Beams under shear: Shear stresses on horizontal planes
Deflections of bent beams: Elastic curve equation
Buckling of compressed beams: Euler's formula for simply supported beams
Design of beams under buckling load
teaching_methods: Teaching material uploaded on Elly platform weekly

assessment_methods.method: Written test (solving exercises and open-ended question)

assessment_rules: The exam is based on a written test, where the student will be asked to solve a few exercises and answer an open-ended question. During the written test, the student can use a calculator and formulary. The evaluation is on a 0-30 scale.
bibliography: F. P. Beer, E. R. Johnston, J. T. DeWolf, D. F. Mazurek, “Meccanica dei solidi. Elementi di scienza delle costruzioni”, McGraw-Hill
